sections.normalized_html:
To find out the boiling temperature of chlorine, we need to calculate [MATH: -24\dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{6}{5}.]

First, we write [MATH: -24\dfrac{1}{3}] as an improper fraction:

[MATH: -24\dfrac{1}{3} = -\dfrac{24\times 3 + 1}{3} = -\dfrac{73}{3}]

Now, we can multiply the two numbers. We multiply the numerators, and we multiply the denominators:

[MATH: (− (73)/(3)) × (6)/(5)|= − (73 × 6)/(3 × 5); = − (73 × 2 × 3)/(3 × 5); = − (73 × 2 × 3)/(3 × 5); = − (73 × 2)/(× 5); = − (146)/(5)]

Finally, we write the resulting improper fraction as a mixed number:

[MATH: -\dfrac{146}{5} = -29\dfrac15]

Therefore, chlorine boils at [MATH: -29\dfrac15{^\circ}\textrm{F}.]
